news.title:
Ashok Leyland expects moderation in LCV, ICV demand from Q4 FY26 levels.
Management anticipates a pickup in heavy-duty trucks, aiding their product mix.

Ashok Leyland faces Q1 FY27 margin pressure due to rising steel costs.
Company plans 1-1.5% price hike and cost controls, but sustained implementation is uncertain.
Final dividend of ₹2.50 announced
news.body: Shareholders will receive a dividend of ₹2.50. Ex-date: 3rd June 2026 Payment date: 26th June 2026 Dividend yield will be 2.3%, which is higher than the industry average of 0.6%. Sustainability & Growth Dividend is covered by earnings (59% earnings payout ratio) but the company has no free cash flows available, indicating it may be using cash reserves or debt to pay the dividend. The dividend has increased by an average of 22% per year over the past 10 years. However, payments have been volatile during that time. EPS is expected to grow by 50% over the next 3 years, which should provide support to the dividend and adequate earnings cover.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹5.91 (vs ₹5.29 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹5.91 (up from ₹5.29 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹563.6b (up 16% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹34.7b (up 12% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 6.2% (down from 6.4% in FY 2025). Revenue is forecast to stay flat during the next 3 years compared to a 12% growth forecast for the Machinery industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 25% per year whereas the company’s share price has increased by 29% per year.

news.title: New minor risk - Earnings quality
news.body: The company has large one-off items impacting its financial results. One-off items were 25% of the size of the rest of the company's trailing 12-month earnings before tax. This is considered a minor risk. One-off items are incomes or expenses that the company does not expect to repeat in future periods. Examples include profits from the sale of a business or expenses from a restructuring or legal settlements. If the company's reported statutory earnings include a large proportion of one-off items it means they may be an unreliable indicator of its true business performance as the earnings were skewed by these incomes or expenses. news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹1.38 (up from ₹1.30 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹148.3b (up 24% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹8.13b (up 6.8% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 5.5% (down from 6.4% in 3Q 2025). Revenue is forecast to grow 2.2% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 13% growth forecast for the Machinery industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 33% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 41% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.

news.title: Ashok Leyland Limited Appoints Alfred Nixon Mendez as Head of Product Development Effective January 2, 2026
news.body: Ashok Leyland Limited announced that Dr. N. Saravanan, previously President & CTO, shall now focus on formulating and driving the company’s strategic product and technology roadmap and partnerships. Mr. Alfred Nixon Mendez, previously Chief Engineer-Global Trucks & Buses, will take over as Head of Product Development with immediate effect, effective January 2, 2026. Mr. Alfred Nixon Mendez has held a distinguished career with Ashok Leyland spanning over the last 32 years. He began his career as a Graduate Engineer Trainee (GET) and played a key role in truck and bus product development, ensuring competitive and innovative offerings including digital transformation initiatives.
